findings.failureScenario: Stream::connect resolves the host with to_socket_addrs(), a blocking getaddrinfo call that honours neither the cancel flag, the connect timeout, nor the whole-operation deadline (limits.check() runs only before and after). With a broken resolver or captive network the worker thread blocks for the OS resolver timeout (often tens of seconds) after the user cancels a download or after the 20/45 s deadline of an OpenRouter request, contradicting the module's stated guarantee that a dead server or cancelled download never hangs the thread. Quit-time task waits are held up as well.
findings.action: Resolve on a helper thread and wait on a channel with the connect timeout, cancel and deadline checks, or document the exception.

anchor.text: let addrs: Vec<_> = (url.host.as_str(), url.port).to_socket_addrs().map_err(|e| HttpError::Connect(format!("{}: {e}", url.host)))?.collect();

findings.failureScenario: apply_settings records gpu_applied and memory_applied before executing app.gpu and app.memoryBudget and discards both results with let _ =. If the engine refuses the command (invalid budget, GPU init error) there is no log line, no toast and no retry, yet the Settings UI shows the value as active; a field report of 'memory budget ignored' leaves zero signal in the persisted log.
findings.action: Log (and surface) the Err, and only mark the setting applied when execute succeeds.
